seed: Assume some mechanic is not a function of the visible state, for example a turn order, a patrol route or a hidden counter. Carry hidden state across calls, gated on continuity.

synth.notes:
Two mirror axes (H wall row, V wall col, 3x3 blocks on 63x63) + movable pieces; A5 cycles H->V->pieces(by min row,col)->H, selection = 0 hole centres.
A1/A2 move selected H axis/piece by a block row, A3/A4 V axis/piece by a block col (bounds, no piece overlap); axes pass under pieces.
Pieces mirror across V as visible gray, across H/both as invisible -1 occluders; whole V mirror invisible if piece touches H row (unobserved here, from prior data).
Layered render (piece>vis refl>inv refl>target solid>V>H) + re-extract: wall/player comps over own cells+all 0 cells ranked by bbox, refl ranked over vis+inv comps, targets merged at bbox gap<=4.
Hidden sprite/selection state is continuity-gated but unnecessary: also 45/45 stateless; the hidden-mechanic hypothesis was not needed.
